answers.why: All Israel are scattered like sheep and told to return each to his house.
Jehoshaphat appoints heads of Israel's families to administer judgment in Jerusalem.
Zebadiah governs the house of Judah in the king's matters.
Jehoshaphat proclaims a fast throughout all Judah, whose inhabitants then gather.
Israel is explicitly called God's people, before whom he displaced the land's inhabitants.
Israel came out of Egypt and refrained from invading the neighboring peoples.
The assembled Levites praise the LORD as the God of Israel.
The enemy armies come against Judah in the battle under Jehoshaphat.
The surrounding kingdoms hear that the LORD fought Israel's enemies.
Jehoshaphat reigns over Judah from Jerusalem for twenty-five years.
Judah is the territory containing the fortified cities given to Jehoshaphat's sons.
Jehoram kills princes of Israel after securing his father's kingdom.
Edom rebels against Judah's dominion and appoints its own king.
Edom's revolt ends its subjection to the kingdom of Judah.
The Philistines and Arabians invade Judah and plunder the king's household.
